name: Toast Notifications
description: Toasts that tell people what just happened without interrupting them: two live regions in the page from the start, errors and toasts with an action that stay until dismissed, timers that pause on hover, focus, and a hidden page, F8 to reach them, and a stack at the bottom that never covers what has focus.

tokens.note: Suggested defaults. The project's design tokens and existing components win.

aiAgentInstructions.summary: Build or extend a toast stack: brief news about something that just happened, read out through two live regions that are in the page from the start (polite, and alert for errors), with errors and toasts with an action staying until dismissed, timers that pause on hover, focus, and a hidden page, F8 to move focus to the newest toast and back, Escape inside a toast, and a stack at the bottom that focus scrolls clear of. Build on the project's toast component when it has a suitable one. Implement only what the task needs, keep existing APIs, and match the project's styling and tokens. The project's conventions win for styling and visual defaults; if one conflicts with an accessibility or correctness requirement in this guide, ask the user instead of choosing silently. Target WCAG 2.2 AA.
keyFeatures: Two live regions in the page from the start, polite and alert, not atomic, never hidden and never nested
Errors and toasts with an action stay until dismissed; the rest leave after about 5 seconds
Timers that pause while the stack is hovered or has focus, or the page is hidden
F8 to the newest toast and back, Escape only inside a toast, and focus returned to where it came from when a toast goes
A stack at the bottom, at most three toasts (one on phones) with the rest shown in order, and focus kept clear of it, also when a toast appears over the focused element
Toasts below modals; a modal's own results show in the modal
implementationSteps: 1. Detect the framework and its version, the styling system, the tokens, and the existing components (projectDetection). If the project already has a toast or notification component, configure or extend it to meet this guide instead of building another one, and keep its API.
2. Check that a toast fits the message (implementationDetails.whenToUse).
3. Build the stack and its live regions (componentSpec.anatomy, frameworkPatterns.toastStack).
4. Add the timing, the keys, and focus (implementationDetails.timing, implementationDetails.keysAndFocus, frameworkPatterns.toastTimers).
5. Place the stack and keep focus clear of it (implementationDetails.stack, implementationDetails.phones), then the optional motion.
6. Check the result against testingChecklist with a keyboard, a screen reader, a phone, and an open modal, and run the project's existing tests and checks.

componentSpec.goal: Tell people what just happened without interrupting them, in a way screen readers announce, keyboard users can reach, and nobody misses for lack of time.

anatomy.hierarchy: section "Notifications" (the stack) → list → toast → icon, title and description, optional action, Dismiss; beside the section, two live regions, polite and alert, that read the toasts out

slotNotes.stack: One <section> named "Notifications" holds the toasts, newest last, at the bottom of the screen: at the inline end on wide screens, and as wide as the screen less 32 px on phones. A top corner would sit over the header's own controls (an account menu, a theme choice) and could hide one entirely when it has focus (2.4.11), so toasts go to the bottom on every screen. On a page with a fixed bottom bar, such as a purchase bar or a tab bar, the script measures the bar and sets --bottom-bar-height to its height, and the stack sits above it, so the bar's controls stay visible.
slotNotes.liveRegions: Two live regions read the toasts out: role="status" (polite), and role="alert" for errors that need attention now; warnings and the rest are polite. Both are in the page, empty, from the start, outside the section, and never hidden: a live region inside a hidden element drops out of the accessibility tree (checked in Chromium). Neither is atomic (aria-atomic="false"): both roles are atomic unless told otherwise, and an atomic region is read out whole each time a message is added, the earlier ones still in it included. Each toast's words go into one of them, and go when the toast goes; the toasts themselves aren't in a live region, so nothing is nested.
slotNotes.buttons: Each toast has a Dismiss button (an icon button named "Dismiss"), and its action is a button named by its visible text ("Undo").

toasts.description: The toasts shown, oldest first: id, variant, title, description, action, and the time left.

waiting.description: Toasts waiting for room, in order; they show while there's room, after a dismissal or when the screen widens, and each is read out when it shows.

paused.description: True while the stack is hovered or has focus, or the page is hidden; the timers keep the time left.

returnFocus.description: The element focus came from when it entered the stack, by F8, Tab, or a click, for F8 again and for the last toast going; the main content when it's gone.

interactions.accessibilityNotes: Focus doesn't move. A toast with an action says "Press F8 for" the action.

interactions.when: the pointer enters or leaves the stack, focus enters or leaves it, or the page is hidden or shown
interactions.accessibilityNotes: Timers go on with the time that was left.
Escape anywhere else is left to dialogs and menus.
If the toast had focus, focus moves to the newest other toast, or back to where it was before it entered the stack, or to the main content.
When the screen narrows, the toasts already showing stay.

interactions.when: it covers the element that has focus
interactions.accessibilityNotes: Scroll padding acts only when something scrolls, so this is done by the script.

interactions.when: the window or an on-screen keyboard brings the stack over the element that has focus
a fixed bottom bar appears, hides, or changes height

responsiveBehavior.phones: On phones, toasts sit at the bottom, one at a time, and their buttons are at least 44 px. Whatever scrolls the page gets a padding-bottom and a scroll-padding-bottom of a fixed bottom bar's height plus, while toasts show, the stack's height and room for a focus ring. That's :root usually; in an app whose page scrolls inside a container, it's that container, with box-sizing: border-box, since otherwise the padding makes a height: 100% container taller than the screen and nothing scrolls (checked). An element that gets focus then scrolls clear of the bar and the stack, and even a short page has room at the end to scroll its last element clear (checked). Where the project already keeps room for its bar at the end of the content, count it once.
responsiveBehavior.wideScreens: At the bottom, at the inline end, 380 px wide, up to three toasts.

variants.success: Polite; leaves on its own unless it has an action.
variants.info: Polite; leaves on its own unless it has an action.
variants.warning: Polite; leaves on its own unless it has an action.
variants.error: Read out through the alert region, and stays until dismissed.

dataContract.showToast: { title, description?, variant: "success" | "info" | "warning" | "error", action?: { label, onSelect }, duration? } — the same shape as most toast libraries' options

exit.properties: opacity; the wrapper's height collapses at the same time

countdownBar.properties: transform: scaleX(), paused with the timer

animations.reducedMotion: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, toasts appear and leave without moving; a short fade is fine.

requirements.1.3.1: The stack is a section named "Notifications"; each toast's buttons are real buttons.
requirements.1.4.1: Each variant has words and an icon, not only a color.
requirements.1.4.11: Icons and the focus ring meet 3:1.
requirements.2.1.1: F8 reaches the toasts, and their buttons work with the keyboard.
requirements.2.2.1: Errors and toasts with an action stay until dismissed; the timers pause on hover, focus, and a hidden page.
requirements.2.4.3: Showing a toast never moves focus; focus returns when a toast with focus goes.
requirements.2.4.11: The stack sits at the bottom, above a fixed bottom bar, and the focused element scrolls clear of both when it gets focus, when a toast appears, when the viewport shrinks, and when the bar appears or changes height.
requirements.2.5.7: Swiping away is optional; Dismiss does the same with a tap.
requirements.4.1.3: Toasts are read out through live regions that are in the page from the start.

keyboardNavigation.f8: F8 moves focus to the newest toast, and F8 again returns it. The section has aria-keyshortcuts="F8", and the read-out of a toast with an action ends with the way to it ("Press F8 for Undo"). Radix uses F8; on many Mac keyboards it needs Fn. A shortcut the project already has for this wins.
keyboardNavigation.inAToast: In a toast, Tab moves between its buttons and Escape dismisses it. Escape anywhere else is left to dialogs and menus.
keyboardNavigation.afterDismiss: When a toast with focus goes, focus moves to the newest other toast, or back to where it was before it entered the stack, by F8, Tab, or a click; F8 back does the same. When that element is gone or can't take focus (removed, disabled, hidden, or made inert), focus goes to the main content: <main> with tabindex="-1", the skip link's target. The script checks that focus really moved.

dismiss.aria-label: "Dismiss" when it shows only an icon

screenReader.announcements: Two live regions read the toasts out: role="status" (polite), and role="alert" for errors that need attention now; warnings and the rest are polite. Both are in the page, empty, from the start, outside the section, and never hidden: a live region inside a hidden element drops out of the accessibility tree (checked in Chromium). Neither is atomic (aria-atomic="false"): both roles are atomic unless told otherwise, and an atomic region is read out whole each time a message is added, the earlier ones still in it included. Each toast's words go into one of them, and go when the toast goes; the toasts themselves aren't in a live region, so nothing is nested.
screenReader.waiting: At most three toasts show at once, one on phones. The rest wait, and show in order when there's room, read out as they show. When the screen narrows, the toasts already showing stay and new ones wait; when it widens, waiting toasts fill the free places in order.

focusManagement.noFocusOnShow: Showing a toast never moves focus.
focusManagement.returnFocus: When a toast with focus goes, focus moves to the newest other toast, or back to where it was before it entered the stack, by F8, Tab, or a click; F8 back does the same. When that element is gone or can't take focus (removed, disabled, hidden, or made inert), focus goes to the main content: <main> with tabindex="-1", the skip link's target. The script checks that focus really moved.
focusManagement.modal: Layers: toasts sit above sticky bars and dropdowns and below modals, in the project's layer scale. While a modal is open, the page behind it is inert, toasts and their live regions included, so the result of the modal's task shows in the modal (the Modal Dialog guide's status message) or after it closes.

framework.description: Find the framework, its version, and how existing components are written before writing code.
detectionSteps: Read the project's dependencies (package.json or its equivalent) for the framework and its version, and use the syntax that version supports.
Open two or three existing components to see their file structure, state handling, and naming.
Look for an existing component that already does this job, in the project or in a design system or UI library it uses, and build on it.

stylingSystem.description: Use the styling system the project already uses, and only that one.
detectionSteps: Check the dependencies and config for the styling setup: Tailwind (version 4 keeps its theme in CSS with @theme, version 3 in tailwind.config.*), CSS Modules, Sass, CSS-in-JS, or plain CSS.
See how existing components apply styles and compose class names, for example with cn or clsx.
Check for design documentation: DESIGN.md, a design system package, or Storybook stories for existing components.
adaptationRules: Write styles the way existing components do, and add no new styling library or system.
With plain CSS, use classes in the project's stylesheets instead of inline styles, except for values computed at runtime.
If the setup is unclear or mixed, ask before choosing.

designTokens.description: Use the project's tokens for color, spacing, radius, type, shadows, motion, and layering.
detectionSteps: Find the tokens: CSS custom properties, a Tailwind theme (@theme or config), a theme object, or a tokens file.
Use them instead of this guide's example values; where there are none, match the closest existing components.
Check that the colors you use meet the contrast minimums: 4.5:1 for text, and 3:1 for focus indicators, icons, and control boundaries.

frameworkPatterns.note: Short snippets in plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the parts that are easiest to get wrong; adapt them to the project's framework and its version.

toastStack.description: The stack, its two live regions (neither atomic), and showToast(): a toast's words go to the alert region for errors and to the polite one otherwise, and a toast with an action says how to reach it; errors and toasts with an action get no timer; at most three toasts (one on phones), the rest shown in order while there's room, after a dismissal and when the screen widens, with the toasts already showing kept when it narrows; and focus moved to the newest other toast, back to where it came from, or to the main content when that can't take it, when a toast with focus goes. The CSS puts the stack at the bottom, at the inline end, above a fixed bottom bar (--bottom-bar-height, which the timers' script measures), and keeps focus clear of both with scroll padding and room at the end of the page.

toastTimers.description: Goes with toastStack: the timers pause while the stack is hovered or has focus, or the page is hidden, and go on with the time that was left; however focus enters the stack, where it came from is remembered; F8 moves focus to the newest toast and back; Escape dismisses the toast that has focus; and the stack's height goes to the padding, with the focused element scrolled clear when the stack appears or grows, or the viewport shrinks, over it; and a fixed bottom bar is measured, padding included, so the stack stays above it and focus scrolls clear of both again when it appears, hides, or changes height.

implementationDetails.whenToUse: A toast is brief news about something that just happened, often with one action: "Message sent", "File deleted" with Undo, "Link copied". Errors people must fix show next to what they concern, as in the Form Validation guide; anything people must read or decide before going on is a dialog. Repeats are grouped ("3 files deleted"), and the same message within a second or so shows once.
implementationDetails.stack: One <section> named "Notifications" holds the toasts, newest last, at the bottom of the screen: at the inline end on wide screens, and as wide as the screen less 32 px on phones. A top corner would sit over the header's own controls (an account menu, a theme choice) and could hide one entirely when it has focus (2.4.11), so toasts go to the bottom on every screen. On a page with a fixed bottom bar, such as a purchase bar or a tab bar, the script measures the bar and sets --bottom-bar-height to its height, and the stack sits above it, so the bar's controls stay visible. Two live regions read the toasts out: role="status" (polite), and role="alert" for errors that need attention now; warnings and the rest are polite. Both are in the page, empty, from the start, outside the section, and never hidden: a live region inside a hidden element drops out of the accessibility tree (checked in Chromium). Neither is atomic (aria-atomic="false"): both roles are atomic unless told otherwise, and an atomic region is read out whole each time a message is added, the earlier ones still in it included. Each toast's words go into one of them, and go when the toast goes; the toasts themselves aren't in a live region, so nothing is nested. At most three toasts show at once, one on phones. The rest wait, and show in order when there's room, read out as they show. When the screen narrows, the toasts already showing stay and new ones wait; when it widens, waiting toasts fill the free places in order. Layers: toasts sit above sticky bars and dropdowns and below modals, in the project's layer scale. While a modal is open, the page behind it is inert, toasts and their live regions included, so the result of the modal's task shows in the modal (the Modal Dialog guide's status message) or after it closes.
implementationDetails.timing: Errors and toasts with an action stay until they're dismissed: an Undo that disappears before a keyboard or screen reader user reaches it fails 2.2.1. The others leave after about 5 seconds (4 to 6 suggested, longer for longer text). The timers pause while the pointer is over the stack, while focus is in it, and while the page is hidden, and go on with the time that was left. Dismissing a toast is silent; it just goes.
implementationDetails.keysAndFocus: Showing a toast never moves focus. F8 moves focus to the newest toast, and F8 again returns it. The section has aria-keyshortcuts="F8", and the read-out of a toast with an action ends with the way to it ("Press F8 for Undo"). Radix uses F8; on many Mac keyboards it needs Fn. A shortcut the project already has for this wins. In a toast, Tab moves between its buttons and Escape dismisses it. Escape anywhere else is left to dialogs and menus. When a toast with focus goes, focus moves to the newest other toast, or back to where it was before it entered the stack, by F8, Tab, or a click; F8 back does the same. When that element is gone or can't take focus (removed, disabled, hidden, or made inert), focus goes to the main content: <main> with tabindex="-1", the skip link's target. The script checks that focus really moved. Each toast has a Dismiss button (an icon button named "Dismiss"), and its action is a button named by its visible text ("Undo").
implementationDetails.phones: On phones, toasts sit at the bottom, one at a time, and their buttons are at least 44 px. Whatever scrolls the page gets a padding-bottom and a scroll-padding-bottom of a fixed bottom bar's height plus, while toasts show, the stack's height and room for a focus ring. That's :root usually; in an app whose page scrolls inside a container, it's that container, with box-sizing: border-box, since otherwise the padding makes a height: 100% container taller than the screen and nothing scrolls (checked). An element that gets focus then scrolls clear of the bar and the stack, and even a short page has room at the end to scroll its last element clear (checked). Where the project already keeps room for its bar at the end of the content, count it once. Scroll padding acts only when something scrolls, so when a toast appears, the stack grows, the bar changes, or the viewport shrinks (the window, or an on-screen keyboard), and the stack or the bar comes over the element that already has focus, the script scrolls that element clear of both (checked in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit, in the page and in an app's scroll container). Focus inside the stack or the bar stays put. The script measures the bar (.bottom-bar, the project's own selector) with a ResizeObserver on its border box, so padding counts: when the bar appears, hides (with hidden), or changes height, as when its text wraps or its padding makes room for a phone's home indicator, the stack moves above it, and the focused element scrolls clear of the stack and the bar, even when the bar grows past where the stack was (checked). The bar is in the page from the start, and several things fixed at the bottom, such as a tab bar and a cookie banner, go in one fixed container, which is what the script measures. This covers the page scrolling, an app's scroll container, a fixed bottom bar, and changes of the viewport's size. Swiping a toast away is optional; its Dismiss button does the same with a tap (2.5.7).
implementationDetails.motion: Motion is optional: a toast slides in over 250 ms and fades out over 200 ms. When one leaves, its wrapper's height collapses at the same time, so the others move into place without a jump. The snippet shows only the entrance. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, toasts appear and leave without moving; a short fade is fine. A countdown bar is optional. It animates transform: scaleX(), not width, and pauses with the timer.
implementationDetails.appearance: Suggested defaults; the project's design and tokens win. Toasts 380 px wide (the screen less 32 px on phones), 12 to 16 px of padding, a 10 px radius, and 12 px apart. Each variant has words and an icon, not only a color. Text meets 4.5:1 and icons 3:1 against the toast: on light tints, use the darkest shades for text (#14532d on #f0fdf4 is 8.7:1) and a dark shade for icons (#15803d, 4.8:1), since green-600 text on a green tint is only 3.0 to 3.2:1. Check the project's own colors in both themes.

edgeCases.longText: Long text wraps; it's never cut off with an ellipsis.
edgeCases.bursts: Many toasts at once: three show, the rest wait in order, and the same message within a second or so shows once.
edgeCases.failedAction: An action that fails, such as an Undo after the item is gone for good, shows its own error toast.
edgeCases.navigation: Toasts can be cleared when the page changes; errors stay.
edgeCases.offline: Offline: one toast that stays while the connection is down, then a brief "Back online".

must: Build on the project's toast component when it has a suitable one, and keep its API
Read toasts out through two live regions that are in the page from the start, never hidden, and not atomic
Keep errors and toasts with an action until they're dismissed, and pause the timers on hover, focus, and a hidden page
Reach the toasts with F8, handle Escape only inside a toast, and return focus to where it came from when a toast with focus goes
Use the project's framework version, styling system, and tokens, the way existing components do
mustNot: Move focus when a toast shows
Nest live regions, or put them inside the hidden stack
Put the stack above modals, or in a top corner over the header
Use toasts for errors people must fix in a form
Add a dependency, such as a toast library, without asking
Use inline styles for static values in a plain-CSS project, or hardcode colors the project has tokens for

testingChecklist: Toasts are for brief news about something that just happened; errors people must fix show next to what they concern, and anything they must read before going on is a dialog
Two live regions, neither atomic, are in the page, empty, from the start and are never hidden: errors go to the alert region, everything else to the polite one
Each toast is read out once, its title and description together; a toast that waits for room is read out when it shows
Errors and toasts with an action stay until they're dismissed; the others leave after about 5 seconds
Timers pause while the stack is hovered or has focus, or the page is hidden, and go on with the time that was left
Showing a toast never moves focus
F8 moves focus to the newest toast and back, and the read-out of a toast with an action says so
Escape dismisses the toast that has focus and does nothing elsewhere
When a toast with focus goes, focus moves to the newest other toast, or back to where it was before it entered the stack, or to the main content when that element is gone or can't take focus
Every toast has a Dismiss button, and an action button named by its visible text
Toasts stack at the bottom, at most three at once (one on phones); the rest wait and show in order when there's room, and the toasts already showing stay when the screen narrows

While toasts show, neither the stack nor a fixed bottom bar hides the focused element, in the page or an app's scroll container: it scrolls clear of both when it gets focus, when a toast appears, when the viewport shrinks, and when the bar appears or changes height, with room at the end of the content for both; the stack sits above the bar and never covers the header
While a modal is open, the result of its task shows in the modal, since the page outside is inert
Long text wraps and is never cut off; text meets 4.5:1 and icons 3:1, and each variant has words and an icon, not only a color
Under reduced motion, toasts appear and leave without moving
Styles come from the project's styling system and tokens
